wonder/statue-of-zeus.subject: a colossal seated statue inside a columned temple hall
wonder/statue-of-zeus.promptAmend: Keep attempt 3's composition exactly: the open hall of six slender lapis columns with plain leaf-scroll capitals and a flat blue-and-gold patterned roof beam, whole inside the frame with wide ivory paper above. Keep the plain rosette pedestal, the three small visitors standing and talking in front, the small domed kiosks on pastel hills at both sides, and the cypresses. Change three things. (1) The roof line: end the roof beam with a plain moulded cornice and at most three small plain gold balls on short stems; no fleur-de-lis, no lily, spearhead, crescent, cross or any other emblem shape. (2) The statue: make it plainly a carved statue of a mature man. Give him a short rounded beard and short wavy hair, a plain thin circlet with no jewels, and a calm simple miniature face (almond eyes, a short ink line for nose and mouth). Paint his skin the same flat pale ivory as the stone throne and pedestal, so the figure, throne and plinth read as one sculpted object, and paint his robe in flat saffron with dark ink fold lines and no tonal shading. Seat him on a tall plain plinth whose top is above the visitors' heads, and scale him so his head nearly reaches the ceiling beam. (3) The pool: a flat rectangle tilted up toward the viewer with parallel sides, not narrowing toward the hall, still flat lapis with fine ripple lines and no reflection.
reasons: The three roof finials are gold fleurs-de-lis, a European heraldic emblem, and they are visible even at the 480x320 thumbnail. art/style.md forbids political, national and heraldic emblems on buildings, and the emblem is also foreign to the idiom.

The colossal figure no longer reads as a statue. It is painted as a living young woman: flesh-toned skin, a long braid, a fine-featured, lightly modelled face and a jewelled circlet. At thumbnail size it looks like a giant person enthroned in a pavilion, not a colossal seated statue. Round 2 asked for a calm bearded man.
The pool is drawn as a trapezoid narrowing toward the hall, a slight converging perspective, where the flat tilted-up rectangle used in the approved mausoleum is what the idiom wants.

Round 2's fixes held and should be kept. The open hall of six lapis columns with plain leaf capitals is whole, with wide paper above. The rosette pedestal and the plain staff and olive branch are right. Three visitors stand and talk, with nobody kneeling. The pool is flat lapis with ripples and no reflection. The side pavilions are small domed kiosks. Margins are wide (band 99.7%), and saffron dominates.
